model: P&C insurer FCFE at cost of equity, net debt held at zero (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 3yr CAGR (153%) is off the FY2022 trough (EPS $1.19 on a 95.8 CR plus $1.9bn investment losses) and is not a growth rate. Equity CAGRs understate economic compounding because PGR pays out most earnings through the annual variable dividend (FY2025 year-end equity is net of the $8.0bn December-declared dividend). Revenue 3/5yr CAGRs (20.9%/15.5%) reflect the 2023-2025 hard-market rate cycle (rate + 10% annual PIF growth) and are not projected forward; forward base growth is 3.5-6.5%.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs use reported OCF-capex, which for an insurer is dominated by float build; they are shown for completeness only and not used. SBC is ~0.15% of revenue and flat in dollars ($121M/$122M/$132M FY2023-25), so the SBC adjustment does not move any CAGR.

scenario_narratives.base: Normalisation, not collapse: FY2026 is the last year of exceptional margins (~88 CR), the CR reverts to PGR's ~92 ten-year average by FY2028 as the soft market and heavy advertising bite, and growth slows to 4.5-5% before re-accelerating with the next hard cycle. Most earnings are distributed (variable dividend + buybacks); ~1.1-2% of revenue is retained to fund premium growth at a 3:1 premiums-to-surplus target.
scenario_narratives.bull: PGR's telematics and segmentation edge keeps it at a ~90 CR through a shallow soft market while property and small-commercial add growth; revenue compounds ~7% for four years and the market keeps paying ~17x distributable earnings.
scenario_narratives.bear: Loss-cost inflation and competitor re-pricing push the CR to ~95-96 for two years (2022 echo), growth stalls at ~2%, and the through-cycle CR settles at ~94; the market re-rates PGR to ~12x.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value PGR on what it can distribute to shareholders after funding premium growth, discounted at the cost of equity. The key judgment is the through-cycle combined ratio: every 1pt of CR is ~0.95pt of pretax margin, ~$800M of after-tax earnings on FY2025 revenue and roughly $22-25/share of base value. The base case assumes PGR's ten-year average CR (~92), not the 87-88 of 2025-26 nor its 96 ceiling.
key_risks_to_valuation: Combined ratio: a 2pt miss on the through-cycle CR (92 -> 94) moves base value by ~$45/share
Soft-market growth: rate cuts plus record advertising spend could slow premium growth below 4% while compressing margin
Catastrophe/weather volatility in property and auto physical damage (Q3-2026 derecho/hurricane quarter)
Loss-cost inflation (parts tariffs, used-car values, medical, litigation) outrunning rate filings and regulatory approval lag
Investment portfolio: NII is ~4% of revenue; falling yields would trim margin ~0.3-0.5pt; mark-to-market on a 3.4-year duration book hits book value not the flows
Capital intensity: if regulators or rating agencies push premiums-to-surplus below 3:1, retention per $ of growth rises and distributable FCFE falls

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 189.20-247.49
data_sources.financials: SEC EDGAR XBRL companyfacts (CIK 80661): FY2025 10-K (0000080661-26-000086) and Q2-2026 10-Q (0000080661-26-000308) -- pretax income, tax, investment gains, SBC, debt, dividends, NPE/NPW, statutory surplus; 10-Q cash flow statement and capital-resources MD&A for buybacks, debt issuance, holdco capital; FY2025 shareholder letter (10-K exhibit 99) for CR 87.4, NPW +12%, PIF +10%; research/PGR/Reports/PGR_Metrics.csv for revenue/NI/EPS/equity history.

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 total revenues $87,671M less net realized/unrealized investment gains $727M (FY2025 10-K XBRL RealizedInvestmentGainsLosses). Gains are mark-to-market noise, not a compounding revenue stream. Net premiums earned $81,661M (94%), net investment income $3,549M (4%), fees/service revenues the rest.
inputs.share_count_basis: 581,371,770 common shares outstanding at 2026-07-02 (Q2-2026 10-Q cover, dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding) plus ~1.2M dilutive RSUs (Q2-2026 diluted 584.2M vs basic 583.0M weighted) = 582.6M fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows and PGR's stated policy is to repurchase shares to neutralize equity-award dilution in the year of grant; opportunistic buybacks beyond that are a use of the FCFE, not an extra value source.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY0 FCFE proxy, NOT owner FCF: FY2025 pretax income $14,223M less $727M investment gains = $13,496M (already after $132M SBC and $278M interest), taxed at 21% = $10,662M, less equity retained to back FY2025 premium growth (0.33 x $11,836M ex-gains revenue growth = $3,906M) = $6,756M distributable.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: OCF $17,548M less capex $348M (FY2025). Meaningless for an insurer: operating cash flow includes float build (unearned premium and loss reserve growth) that is invested in the portfolio and backs policyholder liabilities, not free to shareholders.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K: AllocatedShareBasedCompensationExpense $132M (FY2024 $122M, FY2023 $121M); treasury shares acquired for restricted-stock tax liabilities $92M (FY2025 parent cash flow, 10-K Schedule II). The flows charge SBC expense only (0.15% of revenue); the withholding buyback is the cash settlement of the same expensed award and adding it again with a flat share count would double-count.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025: $74M open market + $92M for equity-award tax withholding. H1-2026: $1,048M open market + $44M withholding (5.4M shares, ~$1.1bn) under the May-2026 25M-share authorization. Authorizations are not spend; only financing-line cash counted.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of EQUITY 8.5%, not a WACC, because the flows are post-interest FCFE (holdco interest $278M FY2025, ~$350M run-rate after the March-2026 $1.5bn senior notes, sits inside the pretax margin). Build: 10-year UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~0.85 (PGR's observed beta is ~0.4-0.6, deliberately rounded up because P&C underwriting margins are cyclical and catastrophe-exposed). USD flows, USD rate. Same rate in all three scenarios: risk is carried in the combined-ratio paths and the probability weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: operating leases immaterial for an insurer; no lease adjustment in flows or bridge.
inputs.net_debt_treatment: Held at ZERO. Senior notes of $8,387M at 2026-06-30 (debt-to-total-capital 19.6%, policy ceiling 30%) are serviced inside the flows; deducting them again after capitalising a post-interest stream would count the debt twice. The ~$97bn investment portfolio and policyholder reserves are operating items (float), not net cash. The $6.7bn held in the non-insurance holdco subsidiary is NOT added: it includes the 2026 note proceeds, PGR treats it as catastrophe/growth capital, and H1-2026 retained earnings that will fund the January-2027 variable dividend are already in the FY2026 flow.
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE at cost of equity on a US P&C insurer, run through the owner-FCF component engine with net debt at zero -- the IAG.AX / GL precedent (memory: iag-insurance-australia-group, gl-globe-life). The dcf-methods routing table default for insurers is BVPS-compounding x exit P/B; overridden because PGR does not compound book: it distributes most earnings through an annual variable dividend ($13.90/share declared FY2025, ~$8.0bn paid January 2026) so GAAP equity is a distribution-timing artefact (FY2025 year-end equity $30.3bn sits below Q3-2025's $35.4bn purely because the dividend was declared in December), and AOCI swings $1-2bn with rates. The owner-FCF DCF is wrong for the same reasons it is wrong for any insurer: OCF/capex include float. ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = total revenues ex investment gains; ebitda_margin_path = pretax margin before SBC (underwriting margin on NPE + net investment income - interest - other); da_pct = 0; capex_pct_path = equity retained to back premium growth (0.33 of incremental revenue: the 3:1 premiums-to-statutory-surplus target for vehicle lines, ~80% equity-funded given the ~20% debt-to-capital policy, plus a buffer), i.e. 0.33 x g/(1+g) of revenue; cash_tax_rate = 21% (FY2025 effective 20.5%, cash tax paid $3,107M = 21.8% of pretax). MARGIN ANCHORS: FY2025 combined ratio 87.4 -> pretax margin pre-SBC ex gains 15.7%; H1-2026 16.1%; Q2-2026 companywide CR rose 1.1pt YoY on severity and +16% advertising; management target is 'grow as fast as we can at or below a 96 CR'. PGR's 10-year average CR (2016-2025) is ~92, which maps to ~11.8% pretax margin -- that is the base-case through-cycle anchor. The Analysis JSON reports a ~89.3 Q3-2026 CR (derecho/hurricane) from monthly releases; the Q3 10-Q is not yet filed and was not used as an anchor. DATA FIXES NOT MADE: PGR_Metrics.csv TotalDebt reads 0 for FY2021-FY2025 but XBRL DebtLongtermAndShorttermCombinedAmount is $6.9bn (FY2023-FY2025) and $8.4bn (Q2-2026); this needs a make-fix correction by the financial-parser, not a DCF edit.

bear.narrative: A 2022-style loss-cost shock: tariffs on parts, social inflation and severity outrun rate while competitors (GEICO, State Farm) re-price aggressively, so PGR restricts growth (revenue +2% FY2027-28) and the CR drifts to ~95-96 (9-10% pretax margin, the 2021-2023 average) before settling at ~94 rather than returning to 92. Catastrophe-heavy years (Q3-2026 derecho) become the norm in property. Terminal 2.5%, capped at 12x FCFE, the bottom of PGR's post-2010 trading range.

base.narrative: FY2026 revenue +6.5% (H1-2026 revenue ex gains +8%, Q2 NPW +5%, PIF +7%) with a ~88 CR year (H1 strong, Q3 catastrophe-heavy) giving a 15% pretax margin. The 2027-2028 soft turn: PGR has been cutting rates in targeted states and spending heavily on advertising to grow, so premium growth slows to 4.5-5% and the CR mean-reverts to its ~92 ten-year average (11.8% pretax margin) by FY2028 and holds there. Growth re-accelerates to 6% as the cycle hardens again and property/Commercial (Coterie BOP/GL) add volume, then glides to 3.5%. Equity retained to back growth at 0.33x incremental revenue. Terminal at min(Gordon 8.5%/3.0%, 15x FCFE).

bull.narrative: Telematics/pricing edge keeps compounding share: PIF growth stays high single digit as property (41 states green) and Commercial Lines add a second and third engine, revenue +7% through FY2029. The soft market is shallow and PGR's segmentation lets it hold a ~90 CR (13.5% pretax margin) through the cycle, roughly its 2018-2020 and 2024-2025 average. Terminal 3.5% growth (PGR keeps taking ~1pt of share a decade in a ~4% nominal market), capped at 17x FCFE, in line with its 10-year average trading multiple.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 15x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Symmetric 25/50/25 rather than the 15/50/35 house default: FY2025-H1 2026 margins (87-88 CR) are at a cyclical high, Q2-2026 already showed CR deterioration on severity and advertising, and the Analysis flags a ~89 Q3-2026 CR. With the P&C pricing cycle turning, downside to the through-cycle margin is as likely as upside, so bull is not over-weighted. Solvency risk is negligible (debt-to-capital 19.6%, statutory surplus $32.9bn), so bear is a margin case, not a capital case.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
sanity_check.fy_end_month_source: December (fallback: no fiscal_year_end and no annual filing)
